title: The Entropy Bridge
mathematical_role: Use one exact finite family to anchor membership marginals and an independent-copy union calculation, then separate that illustration from imported entropy/coupling theorem terrain.
learning_objective: Read coordinate marginals as normalized element frequencies, compute the marginals of A∪B for independent copies, and preserve the distinction between this example and source-specific optimized coupling arguments.
literal_semantics: A is uniform on the six members of F, so H(A)=log2(6).
For independent A and B, q(i)=P(i∈A∪B)=1-(1-p(i))^2.
The resulting union marginals are q(a)=8/9, q(b)=3/4, and q(c)=5/9.
Union closure ensures A∪B lies in F.
nonliteral_semantics: The independent-copy calculation is an exact illustration and is not asserted to be the coupling used by every imported theorem.
The vertical or horizontal arrangement does not rank papers, constants, or proof methods.

notes: Exact finite-example data are reproduced by tests/test_visual_pedagogy_batch1_candidates.py.
Imported theorem-terrain language remains bounded by the documentary source and does not admit a new external claim.

renderer.version_or_environment: Python 3 standard library; deterministic SVG generator v1
reproducibility_notes: The generator uses no network, randomness, timestamps, fonts embedded as files, or external data.
Repository tests compare generator output byte-for-byte with the committed SVG candidate.

accessibility.alt_text: Uniform random set from the six-set family has marginals two thirds, one half, and one third; independent copies have union marginals eight ninths, three quarters, and five ninths, with a guardrail separating the example from source-specific entropy theorems.
accessibility.long_description: The plate starts with a uniform random member A of the exact six-set family and lists its three coordinate marginals. It then takes an explicitly independent copy B and computes the three marginals of A union B using q=1-(1-p)^2. A lower panel states that rigorous dimension-free positive bounds are known but exact constants and hypotheses are source-specific, and that such results do not by themselves settle the universal one-half conjecture.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: The finite-family marginal and independent-union calculations shown are exact; the broader theorem-terrain statements are documentary scope labels inherited from the programme source.
not_claimed: That all entropy proofs use independent copies
Admission of any external proof beyond its separately governed source record

supersession_reason: Expose the random-set variables, exact marginal frequencies, one transparent independent-copy union calculation, and the boundary between illustration and source-specific coupling theorems.
